To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Lifelong exercise training is associated with reduced age related arterial stiffening, especially in the large central arteries; 2) The effect of exercise training varies according to the site, size and age of the arteries; and 3) There are clear dose effects of exercise on arterial stiffing that are dependent on the size and site of the arteries.
'Lifelong exercise training of >25 years duration is associated with lower arterial stiffness, but the effect of lifelong training on arterial stiffness is dose-dependent.
the effect of exercise on arterial stiffness is dependent on both the size and site of the artery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of lifelong exercise on the arterial stiffening of ageing.
the effects of ageing and exercise on the cardiovascular system.
the effects of exercise on the structure and function of the heart, arteries and veins, and the mechanisms by which these changes occur.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more you exercise, the better it is for your heart, but the less you exercise the worse it is for your arteries.

the effect of lifelong exercise training is dose dependent, but the dose required for each site is not the same and depends on the site and size (and hence the wall tension) of the arterial segment under consideration.
lifelong exercise training of >25 years is necessary to maintain youthful arterial compliance, and the dose response varies with the site and size and age of the artery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exercise training is a very powerful intervention for arterial stiffening in older adults and that it is possible to minimize arterial stiffing with ageing with a dose dependent approach to exercise.

lifelong exercise training has a dose-dependent effect on arterial stiffness, with the largest effect being on the large central arteries (aorta) followed by the medium-sized arteries (carotid) and the smallest effect being on the small sized (brachial) arteries.
the dose of lifelong exercise training necessary to preserve 'youthful' arterial stiffness depends on the size of the artery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise training has the most beneficial effects on large central arteries, but not small peripheral arteries.
lifelong committed exercise is necessary to preserve 'younger' arterial stiffness.
the 'dose' of exercise training is very important in preserving vascular health with ageing, and that this effect is dependent on the site of the artery being studied.
